title: Declare the provider context limit on the durable provider profile revision and serve it through resolveCurrentProviderProfile
description:
THE CORRECTED PREREQUISITE for task-c320c34a's one unmapped matrix item (the provider-backed byte budget), filed by architect-eecf80ed at HEAD d954894, REPLACING the runner-side pair R1 task-60defa08 / R2 task-0f212003 that I filed an hour earlier on the wrong seam. Measured, not inferred:

WHY THE PROBE SEAM WAS WRONG. `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime` (packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-host-runtime.ts, 249 lines) takes `{installedRoot, executablePath}` (claude-runtime-request.ts:182), pins the installed CLI closure by content hash (`pinningMethod: "CONTENT_ADDRESSED_COPY"`, :187) and builds a VERSION-ONLY report whose comment says "proves the version and the pin method, and NOTHING else" (:178-192, `declaredContextLimit: null`). `ProbeClaudeRuntimeInput` is `{port, clock, platformIdentity}` (claude-probe.ts:34-38) — no model, no caller declaration channel. The probe cannot know a model window; its `HOLD_UNKNOWN` / `CONTEXT_LIMIT_DECLARATION: UNSUPPORTED` is a TRUE statement about the CLI runtime and must stay that way. Threading an operator value through request → observe → report → probe → daemon persistence would move, across three packages, a value the daemon already owns durably.

WHERE THE DECLARATION BELONGS. The durable `ProviderProfileRevision` (apps/daemon/src/provider-profile/provider-profile-codec.ts:92-108) already carries `selectedModelId`, `modelSnapshotKind`/`modelSnapshotEvidence`, `reasoningEffort`, `concurrencyCeiling`, `limits` (capture ceilings — stderrBytes/stdoutBytes/tailBytes/timeoutMs, provider-profile-fields.ts:15-24, NOT a context budget), a server-computed `profileDigest`, `profileRevisionId`, and `schemaVersion` (PROVIDER_PROFILE_SCHEMA_VERSION). It is exact-keyed (`hasExactKeys` :42 over PROFILE_*_KEYS) and text-bounded (`boundedText` :51, MAX_PROFILE_TEXT_CHARS 256). `resolveCurrentProviderProfile` (provider-profile-resolver.ts:132) serves it as `ProviderCapabilities` (:42-62), echoing `configurationDigest`, `policyDigest`, `profileDigest` — the SAME reader task-c320c34a's matrix already uses for its configuration-digest cell (comment-3d9deced item 14). The registration writer is provider-profile-registration.ts (`providerProbePayload` :54, `PROVIDER_PROBED_EVENT` :37, `conflictsWithProfileHistory` :148).

DELIVERABLE: the profile revision gains `contextLimit` = `{kind: "CONSERVATIVE_INPUT_BYTES", bytes, source}` | `{kind: "EXACT_TOKENS", tokens, source}` | `{kind: "UNKNOWN"}`, where `source` is a bounded label naming WHERE the number came from (an operator declaration in project configuration, or a model-card window for `selectedModelId` with its stated envelope/reserved-output discount) — the provenance lives IN THE ARTIFACT, not in a commit message (governor hold on the superseded row, msg reopenReason of 60defa08). Absent → `{kind: "UNKNOWN"}`, never a number, never `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_BYTE_BUDGET`, never a capture ceiling. Schema version bumps with the exact-key roster; pre-bump profile revisions decode to `contextLimit: UNKNOWN` by a STATED decision (the honest reading of a revision that predates the field), with a test driving an old-schema revision through the new codec. `resolveCurrentProviderProfile` serves `contextLimit` on `ProviderCapabilities`. Design §14.2: "the adapter declares an exact token limit or conservative total input-byte limit … If neither is trustworthy, policy returns HOLD_UNKNOWN" — this row is that declaration, durable and digest-bound.

NOT IN SCOPE: the runner probe (leave `declaredContextLimit: null` alone — it is true), the context composer (c320c34a), exact tokenization.

CONSUMER (clause 1): task-c320c34a — its composer reads `resolveCurrentProviderProfile(...).contextLimit` for `selectContext`'s `byteBudget` (CONSERVATIVE_INPUT_BYTES.bytes; EXACT_TOKENS without a byte bound refuses until a tokenizer capability exists) and binds "the exact provider context limit used" in provenance; UNKNOWN → the composer refuses HOLD_UNKNOWN. Record its id in the completion record.

SEQUENCING NOTE FOR THE GOVERNOR: R1 task-60defa08 (runner probe declaration) and R2 task-0f212003 (persist the probe's limit in the runtime observation) are superseded by this row and should be retired or archived — their premise (the probe as the declaration seam) is measured false. c320c34a's blockedReason names R1→R2; its unblock condition is now THIS row DONE + 1b0a8477 DONE.

fields.ts 104 -> 158 lines (production cap is 250 target / 400 split; comfortably under). Added, beside the existing admittedLimits/admittedSelection analogs and using the module's OWN primitives — boundedText for source, positiveCount for bytes/tokens, hasExactKeys for shape — so no rule here invents its own vocabulary:

- `ProviderContextLimit` = {kind:"UNKNOWN"} | {bytes, kind:"CONSERVATIVE_INPUT_BYTES", source} | {kind:"EXACT_TOKENS", source, tokens}.
- Three frozen key rosters, one per kind, so exactness is per-VARIANT rather than a union of all keys. This is what makes "EXACT_TOKENS carrying bytes" and "UNKNOWN carrying a source" refuse instead of being silently tolerated — a single flat roster could not have refused either.
- `UNKNOWN_CONTEXT_LIMIT`, one frozen shared value, so nothing downstream can mint a second shape of "we do not know".
- `admittedContextLimit(value): ProviderContextLimit | null`, total and non-throwing like every sibling.

FOUR PROPERTIES I DELIBERATELY BUILT IN, each answering a rail or a DoD clause:
1. `source` is REQUIRED on both declared kinds and there is no branch that drops it — rail 2's "a limit without a source is MALFORMED, not UNKNOWN". The sourceless arms refuse via hasExactKeys before any value is read.
2. NO DEFAULTS ANYWHERE. There is no `??`, no fallback literal, no import of DEFAULT_CONTEXT_BYTE_BUDGET, and no read of limits.stdoutBytes/stderrBytes/tailBytes/timeoutMs in this file. An unreadable declaration returns null and the refusal is the caller's to name.
3. UNKNOWN is exactly one key. `{kind:"UNKNOWN", source:"..."}` refuses rather than being trimmed to UNKNOWN — a trimmed record is a field the operator believes they set, the same reasoning the module's exact-record comment already gives.
4. positiveCount rejects zero, negatives, floats, NaN, Infinity and unsafe integers, so "a context limit of 0 bytes" cannot be declared.

RETURNED VALUES ARE FROZEN AT CREATION here rather than only at seal time. The sibling admitters (admittedLimits, admittedSelection) return unfrozen records that codec.sealed() freezes afterwards; I froze in the admitter instead because the codec freezes its nested records by NAME (`Object.freeze(revision.limits)`, `Object.freeze(revision.selection)`) and contextLimit is OPTIONAL — a named freeze would have to be conditional, and a missed condition is exactly the kind of silent hole the isDeeplyFrozen arm exists to catch. Freezing at the source makes the deep-frozen property hold no matter which path built the revision. Step 5 still freezes it at seal for the decode path's sake; the two are consistent, not competing.

THE TRUTH, measured on three DONE rows (be8d405b, 671585ec, 763c24cf):
1. **`complete_task.summary` — NOT PERSISTED. No field exists.** `'summary' in record == False` on all three. This is the defect that makes "the completion record states X" unscoreable, and it is the one the proposal is actually about.
2. **`qa_approve.summary` — PERSISTED as `reviewSummary`** (1972 / 1878 / 1869 chars on the three rows), just NOT READABLE BACK through any tool — `get_context` does not surface it; a reader can `cat .moe/tasks/<id>.json`. An ergonomics gap, recoverable, and a different fix.

WHY THE DISTINCTION MATTERS FOR THE RULING: a fix for (2) is "expose the existing field"; a fix for (1) is "add a field, or forbid clauses that depend on one". Filed as one defect, the cheap half masks the expensive half — a human could approve exposing `reviewSummary` and believe the completion-record problem closed when nothing about (1) changed.

THE OPERATIVE RULE IS UNCHANGED and rests on (1) alone: architects write "record must state X" clauses against a named durable surface (comment or step note under ~4500 chars); workers put load-bearing claims there; graders never reject on a summary's absence alone; a note at exactly 5000 chars is truncated and its clause is re-derived from artifacts.
